offence_severity: Life imprisonment (Section 302 read with Sections 34, 364-A, 201 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code)
physical_harm: Death by strangulation and cutting of throat by sharp weapon; death by stab injuries in chest and abdomen and head injury caused by blunt force impact
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 302 read with Sections 34, 364-A, 201 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code; finally upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused had planned the kidnapping and murder as they had made ransom demands and concealed the bodies
key_evidence_accepted: Recovery of dead bodies of the deceased and their personal belongings at the instance of the accused and the failure to explain the fact within the exclusive knowledge of the accused is an additional circumstance against them.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, including the recovery of dead bodies and personal belongings of the deceased from places disclosed by the accused, and the conversations overheard by the police officials at the STD booth.
trial_duration: The trial judgment was affirmed by the High Court and the Supreme Court. The dates of offence are not specified in the text, but the trial started after the police report on 24th December 2000. The Supreme Court decision was on 28th November 2014.
legal_representation: For the Appellants: R. S. Suri, Sr. Adv., Ms. Shabana, Ms. Shama Praveen, Harinder Mohan Singh, Advs. For the Respondent: Roopansh Purohit, Dr. Monika Gusain, Ramesh Shokeen, Advs.
investigation_status: Post mortem of dead bodies was conducted and other steps for investigation were completed. The accused were sent up for trial.

appeal_history.trial_court: Conviction and sentence of the appellants were affirmed.
appeal_history.high_court: Conviction and sentence of the appellants were affirmed.
appeal_history.supreme_court: The appeal was dismissed, and the conviction and sentence of the appellants could not be interfered with.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were involved in the kidnapping and murder of Devender Chopra and his son Abhishek Chopra, with the accused providing information leading to the recovery of the dead bodies and personal belongings of the deceased. The prosecution also highlighted the recovery of the bodies from covered gutters and the personal belongings from other places disclosed by the accused, which were fully established.
defence_argument: The defence submitted that there was no legal evidence to sustain the conviction and that the evidence of disclosure statements and recoveries was not reliable.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the accused have a duty to explain facts within their exclusive knowledge, and that the court has a duty to grant interim compensation to victims at every stage of the case.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Rajasthan v. Jaggu Ram (2008) 12 SCC 51; Ankush Shivaji Gaikwad v. State of Maharashtra (2013) 6 SCC 770; Re: Indian Woman says gang-raped on orders of Village Court published on Business and Financial News (2014) 4 SCR 264; Mohammad Haroon v. Union of India (2014) 5 SCC 252; Laxmi v. Union of India (2014) 4 SCC 427; Abdul Rashid v. State of Odisha & Ors. (2014) 1 ILR-CUT-202
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the conviction and sentence of the appellants were justified based on the evidence and the failure of the accused to explain the facts within their exclusive knowledge.
other_sentence_order: The State of Haryana is directed to pay Rs. 10 lakhs as interim compensation to the family of the deceased. The compensation will be payable by the Haryana State Legal Services Authority within one month from receipt of a copy of this order. If the funds are not available, the State of Haryana will make such funds available within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, and the Legal Services Authority will disburse the compensation within one month thereafter.
